prerequisites: Knowledge acquired in the courses of Mathematics

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with the basic elements for the analysis and control of dynamic systems.
Highlight the fundamental problems of automatic control and the importance of mathematical models for the study of dynamical systems.
Introduce the main results concerning dynamic systems in continuous time, with particular attention to 'state concepts, stability, controllability, observability'.
Study linear time invariant dynamic systems in the domain of the Laplace transform, introducing the concepts of 'transfer function, block diagrams, frequency response'.
Introduce the problem of how to act on the input variables of a system, suitably described by a mathematical model, to achieve a particular behavior of the process.
Introduce the main criteria for analysis and control synthesis for linear systems with a single input and a single output.
Give special attention to stability, noise attenuation and reference tracking.
At the end of the course the student will be able to formulate and solve a control problem for systems with one input and one output using the techniques developed in the frequency domain.
Describe various systems (electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, etc.) in precise mathematical terms and analyze them by applying methods learned in class.

syllabus_topics: Classification of dynamic systems, equilibrium, linear systems, linearization, stability
Transfer Functions Definition and properties, representation and parameters, step response, realization
Identification of the frequency response, Bode diagrams
Control in the neighbourhood of an equilibrium
Control system nominal and robust stability
Nyquist criterion, gain margin and margin phase, sensitivity analyzes
Requirements and specifications, methods of synthesis, stabilizing networks
Model and industrial implementation of PID controllers (Proportional-Integral-Derivatives)
Simulation and control with the help of Matlab / Simulink
teaching_methods: Exercise conducted on a laboratory process

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (part 1: analysis of dynamic systems)
Written exam (part 2: analysis of closed-loop dynamic systems and controller synthesis)

assessment_rules: The written exam consists of two parts, with 2 hours for each. It is necessary to obtain at least 18/30 on both parts. The overall evaluation is the average of the grades obtained in the two parts, which can be taken in different appeals. Up to 3 points can be added from Matlab exercises, although the maximum grade can be achieved solely through the written exam.
bibliography: P. Bolzern, R. Scattolini, N. Schiavoni. Fondamenti di controlli automatici. McGraw Hill Italia.
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Elettronica E Informatica (Electronic And Computer Engineering), classe L-8 Classe delle lauree in Ingegneria dell'informazione
